definition: The work product to be tested. Examples include requirements, design, code, test plan, user story, build, website.
The body of knowledge used as the basis for test analysis and design. Any documentation from which requirements of a component or system can be inferred.
An imperfection or deficiency in a work product where it does not meet its requirements or specifications. Also called fault or bug.
An event in which a component or system does not perform a required function within specified limits. A failure is the manifestation of a defect during execution.
A human action that produces an incorrect result. Errors lead to defects which may lead to failures.
The fundamental reason for the occurrence of a problem. Identifying root causes helps prevent recurrence.
An aspect of the test object that can be verified by one or more test cases.
A set of preconditions, inputs, actions (where applicable), expected results and postconditions, developed based on test conditions.
A set of test cases or test procedures that are linked together so that one can follow the other. Often executed together.
A sequence of instructions for the execution of a test, specifying the steps to be taken, in detail.
Confirmation by examination and through provision of objective evidence that specified requirements have been fulfilled. Checks 'are we building it right?'
Confirmation by examination and through provision of objective evidence that the requirements for a specific intended use or application have been fulfilled. Checks 'are we building the right thing?'
A group of test activities that are organized and managed together. Examples: component testing, integration testing, system testing, acceptance testing.
Testing of individual hardware or software components. Also called unit testing. Typically performed by developers.
Testing performed to expose defects in the interfaces and in the interaction between integrated components or systems.
Testing an integrated system to verify that it meets specified requirements. Treats the system as a whole.
Formal testing with respect to user needs, requirements, and business processes. Determines whether a system satisfies acceptance criteria.
Testing to detect defects introduced in existing functionality by changes. Ensures previously working functionality still works.
Testing that confirms that a defect has been successfully fixed. Also called re-testing.
A set of tests run on a new build to confirm that the critical functions work, before extensive testing is performed.
Testing that does not involve the execution of the test object. Includes reviews and static analysis.
Testing that involves the execution of the software of a component or system.
An evaluation of a product or project status to ascertain discrepancies from planned results and to initiate corrective actions. A type of static testing.

A type of peer review that relies on visual examination of documents to detect defects, e.g., violations of development standards and non-conformance to higher-level documents. The most formal type of review.
A type of review in which an author leads members of the review team through a work product and the participants ask questions.
The process of evaluating a component or system without executing it, based on its form, structure, content, or documentation.

A black-box test design technique in which test cases are designed to exercise equivalence partitions. An equivalence partition is a range of values that the test object is expected to handle in the same way.
A black-box test design technique in which test cases are designed based on boundary values. Tests the minimum and maximum values and the values just inside and outside the boundaries.
A black-box test design technique in which test cases are designed to execute the combinations of inputs and stimuli (causes) shown in a decision table.
A black-box test design technique in which test cases are designed to execute valid and invalid state transitions.
The percentage of executable statements executed by a test suite: Statement Coverage = (Executable Statements Executed / Total Executable Statements) × 100%.

The percentage of decision outcomes exercised by a test suite: Branch Coverage = (Decision Outcomes Exercised / Total Decision Outcomes (Branches)) × 100%. 100% branch coverage implies 100% statement coverage.
An experience-based testing technique in which the tester simultaneously designs and executes tests based on what they learn.
A test technique without a formal test procedure. The tester's experience is used to anticipate what defects might be present.
Documentation describing the test objectives, scope, approach, resources, and schedule of testing activities.
Documentation that describes the generic test approach for one or more projects, typically at the organizational level.
The set of conditions for officially starting a defined task. Used to determine when a test activity can begin.
The set of conditions for officially completing a defined task. Used to determine when a test activity is done.
A factor that could result in future negative consequences. In testing, product risk relates to the software quality, and project risk relates to the management and control of the project.
The number of defects identified in a component or system divided by the size of the component or system (e.g., defects per 1000 lines of code).
The use of software to perform or support test activities such as test management, test design, test execution, and test evaluation.
A tool that executes tests against a component or system, and evaluates the outcome against expected results and exit criteria.
In test automation, the ratio of net benefits of automation versus the cost. Must be positive to justify the investment in automation.
Continuous Integration / Continuous Delivery. A practice where code changes are automatically built, tested, and deployed. Test automation is essential for effective CI/CD.
